glosses.notes: 环 can mean a ring or loop, and it can also describe something going around the outside of something else.

examples.sentence: 门口那个环看起来不大，可是老人说以前天天有人碰，所以到了今天，里面还是比外面更亮一点。
老师在图上画了一个红环，让大家先看最外面这一圈怎么走，再回头看里面为什么还有一条更细的小路。
这条旧路一环一环地绕着山往上走，所以第一次来的人如果只顾着看风景，很容易一下就把前面的入口错过了。

example_translations.translation: That ring by the door does not look large, but the old man says people used to touch it every day, so even today the inside is still a little brighter than the outside.
The teacher drew a red ring on the diagram and had everyone first look at how the outer loop went, then look back at why there was another thinner path inside it.
This old road goes upward around the mountain loop by loop, so if first-time visitors focus only on the scenery, it is easy for them to miss the entrance ahead in an instant.

secondary_glosses: to return to the original state
glosses.notes: 还原 means restoring something to its earlier state or reconstructing what it originally looked like.

examples.sentence: 师傅修完这张旧桌子以后，没有急着上新的颜色，而是先想办法把它原来的样子一点一点还原出来。
老师把那张发黄的老照片放大以后，大家才看出来，原来前面那片模糊的地方还原以后是一排站得很整齐的孩子。

examples.meaning_en: to return to the original state
examples.sentence: 导演说这场戏最难的不是怎么拍，而是怎么把那个房间还原到很多年前的样子，让人一看就相信那时候真的有人住过。

example_translations.translation: After repairing the old table, the craftsman did not rush to add a new color, but first tried to restore its original appearance little by little.
Only after the teacher enlarged that yellowed old photo did everyone see that, once the blurred area in front was restored, it turned out to be a row of children standing neatly together.

The director said the hardest part of this scene was not how to film it, but how to restore that room to the way it looked many years ago, so that people would believe at a glance that someone had really lived there then.

glosses.notes: 患 is a formal verb used for suffering from a disease or health condition.

examples.sentence: 医生看完前面的检查以后说，父亲虽然患的是以前就有的病，可是这次只要按时吃药，再多休息一点，后面还是会好一点。
孩子以前从来没患过这种病，所以母亲一听见医生说要先在家里休息几天，马上就把后面的安排全改了。
那位老人年轻时就患过肺上的病，所以一到天气突然变冷的时候，全家人都会比平常更注意他晚上睡得好不好。

example_translations.translation: After reviewing the earlier tests, the doctor said that although Father was suffering from a condition he had already had before, this time things would still get a little better later as long as he took medicine on time and rested a bit more.
The child had never contracted this illness before, so as soon as Mother heard the doctor say he needed to rest at home for a few days first, she changed all the later arrangements.

That older man had already suffered from a lung problem when he was young, so whenever the weather suddenly turns cold, the whole family pays closer attention than usual to whether he sleeps well at night.

glosses.notes: 幻想 can mean imagining something unreal in your mind, or the fantasy itself.

examples.sentence: 他小时候常常幻想自己长大以后能一个人坐船去很远的地方，所以后来第一次真的出门时，反而一点都不觉得害怕。
老师说写故事不是把所有幻想都放进去就行，更难的是让读的人相信，这些看起来不可能的事在那个晚上真的会发生。
经理后来提醒那个年轻人，光靠幻想不会让问题自己变小，还是得先把眼前最急的事一件一件做好，再想后面怎么走。

example_translations.translation: As a child, he often fantasized that after growing up he would be able to take a boat alone to very distant places, so when he later truly left home for the first time, he did not feel afraid at all.

The teacher said that writing a story is not just a matter of putting every fantasy into it; the harder part is making the reader believe that these seemingly impossible things could truly happen that night.

The manager later reminded the young man that relying only on illusion would not make the problem smaller by itself; he still had to handle the most urgent things in front of him one by one before thinking about what to do later.

glosses.notes: 患者 means a patient, especially someone receiving medical treatment or care.

examples.sentence: 医生去病房看那位患者的时候，没有先问机器上的数字，而是先坐下来听他把昨天晚上最难受的那一段慢慢讲完。
医生提醒家属，这位患者刚做完检查以后最好先别马上站起来，不然头一晕，走到门口都不方便。
医院后来把几个年纪大的患者安排到离门口更近的房间，不是因为那里更安静，而是方便他们白天去做检查时少走一点。

example_translations.translation: When the doctor went to the ward to see that patient, he did not ask about the numbers on the machine first, but sat down and listened while the patient slowly finished describing the hardest part of the previous night.

The doctor reminded the family that after this patient had just finished the examination, it was best not to stand up immediately, or if dizziness came, even walking to the doorway would be inconvenient.
The hospital later arranged several older patients in rooms closer to the entrance, not because it was quieter there, but because it made them walk a little less during the day when going for tests.

glosses.notes: 黄 means the color yellow, and it often appears when describing leaves, light, cloth, paper, or old photos.

examples.sentence: 母亲把那件黄衣服找出来的时候，妹妹一下就笑了，因为她小时候最喜欢穿它去学校，可是后来大了以后就不能穿了。
老师把那张有一点发黄的纸拿给大家看时说，别只看它旧，还要想一想它为什么能在这么多年以后还留在这里。
秋天一到，院子里那棵树的叶子就慢慢从绿变黄，所以老人每天早上开门以后，第一件事就是先看看地上又落了多少。

example_translations.translation: When Mother took out that yellow piece of clothing, my younger sister laughed at once, because she had loved wearing it to school when she was little, but after growing older she could no longer wear it.
When the teacher showed everyone that somewhat yellowed sheet of paper, she said not to notice only that it was old, but also to think about why it had still remained here after so many years.

As soon as autumn arrives, the leaves of that tree in the yard slowly turn from green to yellow, so every morning after opening the door, the old man’s first act is to see how many more have fallen to the ground.

glosses.notes: 皇帝 means an emperor, especially in historical stories, museums, and discussions of old dynasties.

examples.sentence: 老师讲到那位皇帝的时候，没有先让大家背他做过什么，而是先问学生，如果自己住在那个时候，最怕听到哪一种命令。
导游说这间屋子以前有皇帝来住，所以里面和外面都和平常不同，连门口站的人也比前面多很多。
孩子看完那部写皇帝的电影以后，最难忘的不是前面那些很大的房子，而是那个小孩子明明很害怕，却还是得一直站在旁边。

example_translations.translation: When the teacher spoke about that emperor, she did not first make everyone memorize what he had done, but asked the students which kind of command they themselves would fear most if they had lived in that era.

The guide said that an emperor once came to stay in this room, so both the inside and the outside were different from usual, and even the number of people standing at the doorway was much greater than before.

After watching that film about an emperor, what the child found hardest to forget was not the large buildings shown earlier, but that the small child, though clearly afraid, still had to keep standing at the side.

glosses.notes: 灰尘 means dust that settles on surfaces, rises in the air, or gathers in old rooms and on old things.

examples.sentence: 这间屋子很久没人住了，所以门一打开，窗边那层灰尘就一下飞起来，连站在后面的人都赶紧把脸转开了。
母亲擦那排旧书的时候最怕灰尘进到眼里，因为只要一难受，后面本来想慢慢整理的事就全得先停下来。
修路那几天门口灰尘一直很大，所以店里的人每天晚上关门以前都得把最外面那一排东西再重新擦一遍。

example_translations.translation: No one had lived in this room for a long time, so the moment the door opened, the layer of dust by the window flew up at once, and even the people standing behind quickly turned their faces away.
When Mother wipes that row of old books, what she fears most is dust getting into her eyes, because once that happens, all the work she had planned to sort through slowly later has to stop first.

During the days when the road was being repaired, the dust at the entrance stayed very heavy, so every evening before closing, the people in the shop had to wipe down the outermost row of things all over again.

glosses.notes: 灰心 describes feeling discouraged and losing confidence after trouble, delay, or repeated failure.

examples.sentence: 他考了两次都没过以后当然有一点灰心，可是老师还是劝他先别急着放弃，因为这次错的地方已经比上次少了很多。
母亲看见孩子坐在桌子前一直不说话，就知道他不是不会做，而是前面改了很多次还没改好，所以一下灰心了。
经理后来提醒大家，前面的问题再多也别灰心，因为只要现在先把最难的几件事做好，后面的路就不会像今天看起来这么乱。

example_translations.translation: After failing twice, he was of course somewhat discouraged, but the teacher still urged him not to give up too quickly, because this time the mistakes were already far fewer than last time.

When Mother saw the child sitting silently at the table, she knew it was not that he could not do it, but that he had changed it many times already without finishing well, so he had suddenly grown downhearted.

The manager later reminded everyone not to lose heart no matter how many problems lay ahead, because as long as the hardest few things were handled well now, the road afterward would not look as chaotic as it did today.

glosses.notes: 回报 means repaying help, kindness, trust, or effort, or giving something back in return.

examples.sentence: 父亲总说别人以前帮过自己的那些事不一定一下能回报完，可是只要心里一直记着，以后总会找到合适的时候。
她这几年一直认真工作，为了让家里过得好一点，也为了回报那个在最难的时候还相信她的人。
老师说读书以后怎么回报这个地方，并不是只有回来上班一种办法，真正重要的是别把以前得到的帮助全忘了。

example_translations.translation: Father always says that the help others once gave him cannot necessarily be repaid all at once, but as long as he keeps it in mind, he will eventually find the right time later.
She has worked seriously these past years both to let life at home become a little better and to repay the person who still believed in her during the hardest time.
The teacher said that there is not only one way to give back to this place after studying; what truly matters is not forgetting all the help one once received.

glosses.notes: 回顾 means looking back over past events, work, or experiences in order to review them.

examples.sentence: 老师在考试以前没有急着讲新的内容，而是先带大家把前面最容易错的几个地方回顾一遍，免得临时又乱了。
节目最后请那位老人回顾自己年轻时第一次出门的日子时，台下原来只想看看热闹的人也慢慢安静下来了。
经理开会时说，这次不是只看结果好不好，还得认真回顾前面哪一步开始慢下来，不然以后还会在同一个地方出问题。

example_translations.translation: Before the exam, the teacher did not hurry to explain new material, but first led everyone in reviewing the few places where mistakes were easiest to make, so that things would not turn chaotic again at the last minute.

At the end of the program, when the elderly man was asked to look back on the days when he first left home in his youth, even the people in the audience who had originally only wanted some excitement gradually quieted down.

At the meeting, the manager said that this time they were not only looking at whether the result was good, but also had to carefully review at which earlier step things began to slow down, or the same problem would arise again later.

glosses.notes: 回头 can mean turning around, doing something later, or in some contexts “if later on”.

examples.sentence: 孩子听见后面有人叫自己的时候没有马上回头，因为他手里那碗汤太满，只要一动，前面那一点就会先洒出来。
你先把最急的那件事做完，别的问题回头再谈也来得及，因为现在门口等着的人已经越来越多了。
回头天气真一下变冷了，母亲还是打算先把老人接到家里住几天，免得夜里一个人起来找药太不方便。

example_translations.translation: When the child heard someone calling from behind, he did not turn around right away because the bowl of soup in his hands was too full, and the slightest movement would have made some spill out first.
You finish the most urgent thing first; the other issues can still be discussed later, because the number of people waiting at the entrance is already growing larger and larger.

If the weather really suddenly turns cold later on, Mother still plans to bring the older person home to stay for a few days first, so that getting up alone at night to look for medicine will not be too inconvenient.

glosses.notes: 汇 can mean sending money or, in another sense, several streams or lines coming together in one place.

examples.sentence: 父亲在外地工作那几年，每个月一发工资就先把一部分钱汇回家里，所以家里后来修房子的时候才没有那么着急。
前面的几条小河到了桥下以后慢慢汇到一起，所以一下大雨，下面那片地方就会比以前更危险。
他怕家里临时要用钱，所以一听见母亲在电话里说老人又得去医院，就马上把手里剩下的钱先汇过去了。

example_translations.translation: During the years when Father worked away from home, he sent part of his pay back home every month as soon as he received it, so later, when the family repaired the house, things were not quite so rushed.
Several small rivers ahead slowly come together after reaching beneath the bridge, so once heavy rain begins, the area below becomes more dangerous than before.

He was afraid the family might suddenly need money, so as soon as he heard Mother say on the phone that the older person had to go to the hospital again, he sent over what money he had left right away.

glosses.notes: 汇报 means giving a report upward or formally explaining the current situation and results.

examples.sentence: 经理进去汇报以前，先在门口把数字又看了一遍，因为只要前面有一点没说清楚，后面的决定就可能全受影响。
医生看完病人以后没有马上离开，而是先把情况简单记下来，准备回去以后再向上面的人做一次完整的汇报。
老师让小组长明天上课时当着大家的面汇报这周做到哪一步，不是想给人压力，而是怕有人一直跟不上又不好意思说。

example_translations.translation: Before going in to report, the manager looked over the numbers once more at the door, because if even a little remained unclear at the start, all the later decisions could be affected.
After seeing the patient, the doctor did not leave immediately, but first briefly wrote down the situation and planned to make a full report to the people above after returning.

The teacher asked the group leader to report in front of everyone tomorrow on how far they had gotten this week, not to put pressure on anyone, but because she feared some people were falling behind and felt too embarrassed to say so.

glosses.notes: 绘画 is a formal word for drawing or painting pictures.

examples.sentence: 她小时候最安静的时候就是一个人坐在窗边绘画，所以母亲后来一看见她把纸和笔拿出来，就知道她心里又想清楚了一些事。
老师带孩子们去看展览以前先说，绘画不是只把眼前看到的东西照着画下来，更难的是让别人看见你心里最在意的地方。
那位老人后来开始认真学绘画，虽然手已经没有年轻时那么好，可是他每天还是会慢慢画很久。

example_translations.translation: The quietest moments of her childhood were when she sat by the window painting alone, so later, whenever Mother saw her take out paper and pens, she knew her mind had begun sorting some things out again.

Before taking the children to the exhibition, the teacher said that drawing is not only a matter of copying what you see in front of you; the harder part is letting others see what matters most to you inside.
That older man later began seriously learning painting. Although his hands were no longer as good as when he was young, he still painted slowly for a long time every day.

glosses.notes: 会见 means meeting someone formally, often for an official, public, or planned purpose.

examples.sentence: 校长下午会见那几位从外地来的老师以前，先让人把学生前面准备的材料放好，免得一进去大家就一下乱了。
那位作家会见读者的时候没有先坐到最前面，而是站在门口一个一个听大家说自己为什么会把这本书看完。
新闻里说那两个人今天下午会见，可是很多人后来真正记住的，不是他们说了什么，而是最后一起走出来时的表情。

example_translations.translation: Before the principal formally met those teachers from outside that afternoon, he first had someone lay out the materials the students had prepared earlier, so that things would not become disorderly the moment everyone went in.
When that writer met the readers, he did not sit in the front first, but stood at the entrance listening one by one as everyone explained why they had ended up finishing the book.

The news said those two people would meet formally this afternoon, but what many people later truly remembered was not what they said, but the expressions on their faces when they finally walked out together.

glosses.notes: 汇款 means sending money to someone, and it can also mean the remittance itself.

examples.sentence: 父亲刚听见家里那边要交住院的钱，就先去银行汇款，因为他怕如果等到第二天，前面的手续又会被拖住。
母亲收到那笔汇款以后没有先给自己买东西，而是先把老人下个月要用的药和孩子上学要交的钱都准备出来。
他原来以为汇款很快就能到，可是后来一问才知道，中间只要有一个地方名字写得不清楚，后面就可能多等好几天。

example_translations.translation: As soon as Father heard that the family back home needed to pay for the hospital stay, he went to the bank to remit money first, because he feared that if he waited until the next day, the earlier procedures would be delayed again.
After Mother received that remittance, she did not buy anything for herself first, but instead prepared the money needed for the older person’s medicine next month and for the child’s school fees.
He had originally thought the remittance would arrive quickly, but later found out that if the name in even one place was written unclearly, there might be a delay of several extra days afterward.

glosses.notes: 婚姻 means marriage as a long-term relationship and shared life between two people.

examples.sentence: 老师说写到婚姻的时候，如果只写两个人最热闹的那一天，其实还不够，真正难写的是他们后面怎么一起过很多普通日子。
她后来知道，好的婚姻不是一点问题都没有，而是婚姻里有了难事以后，双方都愿意先把话说清楚。
那部电影没有把婚姻拍得太轻松，所以看完以后，母亲反而说这才像真的生活，因为前面和后面的压力都没有被故意藏起来。

example_translations.translation: The teacher said that when writing about marriage, it is not enough to describe only the most lively single day of two people’s lives; the truly hard part is showing how they live through many ordinary days together afterward.

She later understood that a good marriage is not one with no problems at all, but one in which, after difficulties arise within the marriage, both sides are willing to speak things through clearly first.

That film did not portray marriage as too easy, so after watching it, Mother instead said it felt more like real life, because neither the earlier nor the later pressures had been deliberately hidden.

glosses.notes: 混 can mean mixing things together, blurring them together, or doing something carelessly without clear order.

examples.sentence: 老师提醒孩子们，别把这两个字混在一起，因为前面看着只有一点不一样，可是真正写到句子里，意思就会一下差很多。
经理后来看表的时候才发现，原来有人把昨天和今天的数混到了一张纸上，所以大家前面才会一直觉得哪里不对。
他那几天心里一直很乱，连吃药的时间都想混过去，可是医生一问前面漏了几次，他自己也知道这样下去不行。

example_translations.translation: The teacher reminded the children not to mix these two characters together, because at first they seem to differ only a little, but once placed in a sentence, the meaning changes a great deal at once.

Only later, when the manager looked at the chart, did he discover that someone had mixed yesterday’s numbers and today’s onto the same sheet, which was why everyone had kept feeling that something was off earlier.

His mind had been in turmoil for several days, and he even wanted to let the times for taking medicine slide by carelessly, but when the doctor asked how many doses he had already missed, he himself knew this could not continue.

glosses.notes: 混合 means combining different things together into one mixture or blend.

examples.sentence: 医生说这两种药不能自己随便混合着吃，因为只要前面一点没问清楚，后面身体的反应就可能比平常大很多。
老师做实验的时候先把两种颜色慢慢混合到一起，让大家看清楚它们不是一下变的，而是中间还有很多细小的变化。
店里后来把老味道和新做法混合起来试了一段时间，因为老板想知道，大家到底更愿意记住以前，还是愿意接受一点新的变化。

example_translations.translation: The doctor said these two medicines cannot simply be mixed and taken together at will, because if even a small point is not clarified beforehand, the body’s later reaction may be much stronger than usual.

During the experiment, the teacher slowly blended two colors together first, letting everyone see clearly that the change did not happen all at once and that many small transitions appeared in between.

Later the shop tried mixing the old flavor and the new method for a period of time, because the owner wanted to know whether people were more willing to remember the past or accept a little new change.

glosses.notes: 混乱 describes a situation that is messy, chaotic, or out of order.

examples.sentence: 门口一下来了太多人以后，前面的队很快就变得有点混乱，所以经理先让大家别往里挤，再一个一个慢慢进去。
他搬家那天家里看着很混乱，可是母亲还是能一下找到孩子晚上要穿的衣服，因为重要的东西她前面都先分开了。
老师说写文章的时候别把时间写得太混乱，不然读的人前面刚明白，后面又会一下不知道事情到底先后怎么发生。

example_translations.translation: After too many people arrived at the entrance all at once, the line in front quickly became somewhat chaotic, so the manager first told everyone not to push inward and then let them go in slowly one by one.
The house looked very disorderly on moving day, but Mother could still immediately find the clothes the child needed that evening, because she had separated the important things earlier.

The teacher said not to write time too chaotically in an essay, or the reader will just begin to understand the earlier part and then suddenly lose track of what happened first and what happened later.

glosses.notes: 活力 means vitality or lively energy in a person, a place, or an activity.

examples.sentence: 这条老街白天看着很普通，可是一到晚上灯都亮起来，门口的人慢慢多了以后，整条路就有了一种新的活力。
医生让父亲别着急上班，不是因为病已经很重，而是因为现在身体的活力还没完全回来，太早用力只会更慢。
老师说孩子画里最打动人的地方，不是颜色有多亮，而是那几个人站在雨里还是不肯走开的样子很有活力。

example_translations.translation: This old street looks ordinary in the daytime, but once the lights come on at night and more people gradually appear at the entrances, the whole road takes on a new kind of vitality.

The doctor told Father not to hurry back to work, not because the illness had grown very severe, but because the body’s vitality had not yet fully returned and pushing too soon would only slow recovery further.
The teacher said the most moving part of the child’s painting was not how bright the colors were, but that the few people standing in the rain and still refusing to leave seemed full of vitality.

glosses.notes: 活跃 means active, lively, or dynamic, whether for people, discussion, a market, or an atmosphere.

examples.sentence: 这个孩子平常一到台上就特别活跃，所以老师前面一看见他突然安静下来，就知道他心里一定是有了什么事。
最近这个地方晚上比以前活跃多了，不只是因为新店开得多，也是因为年轻人下班以后开始愿意在这条路上慢慢走一会儿。
老师一提到那个大家都熟的故事，原来坐在后面一直不说话的人也一下活跃起来，连平常最少发言的人都开始举手。

example_translations.translation: This child is usually especially active the moment he gets on stage, so when the teacher saw him suddenly grow quiet earlier, she knew something must be on his mind.

Lately this area has grown much more dynamic at night than before, not only because more new shops have opened, but also because young people have started to be willing to stroll slowly along this road after work.

As soon as the teacher brought up that story everyone knew, even the people sitting in back who had stayed silent began to grow active at once, and even those who usually spoke the least started raising their hands.

glosses.notes: 火柴 means a match used to start a flame.

examples.sentence: 外公家里一直有火柴，一到晚上他还是把它放在门口，因为前面要是一下黑了，大家都能先看见东西。
孩子第一次看见母亲划火柴的时候一直站得很近，所以父亲赶紧把他往后拉一点，怕那一点火一下碰到手。
那间旧屋子里虽然还有火柴，可是老师先提醒大家别自己去碰，因为门一打开以后，里面的味道已经和以前完全不同了。

example_translations.translation: There have always been matches in Grandpa’s home, and each evening he still puts them by the doorway, because if things suddenly go dark ahead, everyone can first see what is around them.
The first time the child saw Mother strike a match, he stood very close, so Father quickly pulled him a little farther back, afraid that that small flame might touch his hand all at once.

Although there were still matches in that old room, the teacher first reminded everyone not to touch them by themselves, because once the door was opened, the smell inside had already become completely different from before.

glosses.notes: 火灾 means a destructive fire accident or fire disaster.

examples.sentence: 新闻里说那场火灾来得太快，所以楼里很多人前面还以为只是小问题，后来一听见门外一直有人喊，才知道得马上往下走。
老师讲到那次火灾的时候，没有先说损失有多大，而是先让大家想一想，如果晚上家里突然停电，自己最先该做什么。
那条旧街后来重新开起来以后，很多人还是会记得前面的火灾，因为它不只是烧掉了房子，也一下让不少人把从前的日子全想起来了。

example_translations.translation: The news said that fire disaster came too quickly, so many people in the building had first thought it was only a small problem; only later, when they heard people shouting outside the door, did they realize they had to go downstairs immediately.

When the teacher spoke about that fire, she did not first talk about how great the losses were, but instead had everyone think about what they themselves should do first if the power suddenly went out at home at night.

After that old street reopened later, many people still remembered the earlier fire disaster, because it had not only burned down houses, but also suddenly brought back the memory of earlier days for many people.
